data.description:
## Observation
In Windows sweep run 44456347985 (job 135332660982, main at ab323f7df0c), `tests/unit/reconciler/apply/test_bridge_state_atomic_write_concurrency.py::test_peer_confirmations_distinct_concurrent_saves_are_merged` failed with `PermissionError(13, 'Permission denied')` recorded by the test's concurrent READER thread (`final_path.read_text()`, `:43-47`), not by the writers. The writers now retry a contended replace (`rebar._store.fsutil.replace_with_retry`, sporting-feudalist-bluet). On Windows, opening a file while `MoveFileEx(MOVEFILE_REPLACE_EXISTING)` replaces it can fail with access denied; POSIX readers never see this.

## Hypotheses (unproven)
- Product readers that open a published sidecar, cache or cursor without holding the writer's lock (for example a store's initial load) can get the same transient `PermissionError` on Windows and treat it as a failed or empty read.
- Readers that already read under the sibling lock (`sidecar_transactions.mutate_json_object`) are unaffected.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The product read paths of files published through `atomic_write`/`replace_with_retry` are enumerated, and each is recorded as either lock-protected or exposed on Windows.
- [ ] Every exposed read path tolerates the transient refusal (or is shown not to need to), with a Windows-branch unit test.
data.title: Windows: readers of an atomically replaced file can get PermissionError while a replace is in flight
